label: sf-station/sf-elevator-door

answer.main_body: elevator door and frame with floor indicator
answer.evidence: The elevator is drawn entirely as a flat architectural front elevation. The upper white section contains the floor indicator display facing directly forward, functioning as the front lintel/transom rather than a horizontal top surface, and neither the frame lintel nor the door threshold shows any foreshortened top plane.
The elevator structure features a distinct 6-row trapezoidal top surface/slanted lintel cap (rows 1-6) visible from the 3/4 top-down angle above the vertical door frame (rows 8-30).

The top of the elevator frame recedes as a trapezoid spanning rows 1 to 7 (with sides tapering inward toward the back edge at row 0/1), showing clear 3/4 view top surface depth above the vertical front face.

answer.main_body: elevator entrance frame and sliding doors
answer.evidence: The elevator structure features a distinct, foreshortened top surface across rows 1–6 rendered in a significantly lighter value than the south-facing door frame (rows 9–30), tapering trapezoidally toward the rear edge.
